title: Estimation and Inference for the $\tau$-Quantile of Heterogeneous Individual-Specific Coefficient
abstract: arXiv:2605.01923v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We study quantiles of heterogeneous coefficients across the $n$ observed units of a panel. Treating the coefficients as deterministic, we estimate each from $T$ observations, then use the estimates and their standard errors to construct a smoothed quantile estimator and estimate its variance. When $T^{1/2}\ll n\ll T^{3/2}$, the estimator is asymptotically normal around a deterministic center. A feasible bias correction relaxes the sample growth restriction to $n/T^{3/2}\to c\in[0,\infty)$, accommodating panels with large $n$. Normal inference extends to the target quantile when the difference between the deterministic center and the target is negligible relative to the standard error. Without this restriction, we establish an impossibility result that the distribution of the studentized error relative to the target cannot be estimated uniformly consistently. For practical inference in this case, we construct a conservative interval w

translated_title: 异质个体特定系数 τ 分位数的估计与推断
translated_abstract: 我们研究面板数据中 n 个观测单元之间异质系数的分位数。将系数视为确定性变量，我们利用每个个体的 T 个观测对其进行估计，然后基于这些估计值及其标准误构建一个平滑分位数估计量，并估计其方差。当 $T^{1/2}\ll n\ll T^{3/2}$ 时，该估计量围绕一个确定性中心渐近正态。一种可行的偏差修正将样本增长限制放宽为 $n/T^{3/2}\to c\in[0,\infty)$，从而适用于 n 较大的面板。当确定性中心与目标分位数之间的差异相对于标准误可忽略时，正态推断可扩展至目标分位数。在不施加这一限制的情况下，我们建立了一个不可能性结果：相对于目标的学生化误差的分布无法被均匀一致地估计。针对这种情况下的实际推断，我们构造了一个保守区间……
tldr: 本文提出针对面板数据中异质个体特定系数 τ 分位数的平滑估计量及其方差估计，通过可行的偏差修正放宽样本增长条件以实现渐近正态推断，并证明了当中心与目标分位数偏离不可忽略时学生化误差分布无法被均匀一致估计的不可能性结果，据此构造了保守推断区间。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a smoothed quantile estimator for heterogeneous individual-specific panel coefficients with feasible bias correction enabling asymptotic normal inference, establishes an impossibility result that the studentized error distribution cannot be uniformly consistently estimated when the center deviates from the target quantile, and constructs conservative intervals for practical inference.
